definition: Building software primarily by describing what you want in natural language and letting an AI write the code, with the human steering rather than typing every line.
details: Popularized by Andrej Karpathy in 2025, the term describes a flow where the developer prompts, reviews and iterates on AI-generated code — “fully giving in to the vibes” — while the model handles syntax, boilerplate and edits.

explainer.lead: Vibe Coding is building software mainly by describing what you want in natural language and letting an AI write the code, with the human steering rather than typing every line. It shifts the developer's work from writing syntax to prompting, reviewing, and iterating.

tiers.eli5: Instead of typing every instruction yourself, you tell the computer what you want in plain words and it writes the code, while you check it and say what to change.
tiers.practitioner: Developers prompt, review, and iterate on AI-generated code while the model handles syntax, boilerplate, and edits. The pitfall is steering without reading every line, which makes review discipline essential.
tiers.paperLevel: Described in 2025 by Andrej Karpathy as a flow of prompting, reviewing, and iterating on model-generated code — "fully giving in to the vibes" — with the model handling syntax, boilerplate, and edits. It is a workflow description, not a formal method with stated limits.

explainer.example: A developer describes the app they want in plain language, the AI writes the code, and the developer reviews the result and asks for changes.
